subject: Private control plane — SAML/SCIM assertion patterns and role provisioning flow
messages:
From: IT Admin <it-admin@acme-financial.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-15T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Private CP: SAML/SCIM role mapping and delegated provisioning questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team wants clarity on how Redwood handles identity & role assertions for a private control plane in our VPC. A few specific asks to help with our internal architecture review: 

- What SAML attributes do you recommend for conveying roles vs groups? We use Okta and currently map roles via a claim called `app_role`.
- For SCIM, do you require push provisioning (SCIM 2.0 push) or can you consume group membership via SAML assertions only?
- How do you handle operator/service accounts vs human users? Any preferred NameID or subject formats?
- Audit & retention: what audit logs related to admin role grants and authentication do you capture and how long do you retain them for Private CP?
- Do you have a recommended cutover pattern (canary vs wholesale) for customers migrating from IdP-managed roles to SCIM-managed roles?

We can share our Okta metadata if that helps — aim to start an integration window later this month.

Thanks,
Ahmed
IT Admin — Acme Financial Services
attachments: none
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: IT Admin <it-admin@acme-financial.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-15T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private CP: SAML/SCIM role mapping and delegated provisioning questions

Ahmed — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I attached a short design sketch (priv_access_design_v1.pdf) with examples and a recommended mapping. Mina and Karthik are looped for technical specifics.

Quick answers: 
- SAML attributes: use email (or persistent NameID), groups, and one role claim (we recommend `rdw_role`). `rdw_role` should carry the canonical role name we map to internal entitlements (e.g., `admin`, `operator`, `view_only`). If you already have `app_role` we can map that to `rdw_role` in the metadata mapping.
- SCIM: We support SCIM 2.0 push provisioning for users/groups and attributes (recommended for controlled production). SAML group-only approaches are supported for read-only membership but lack lifecycle synchronization (we'll see stale members). For Private CP we recommend SCIM push + SAML for SSO.
- Operator/service accounts: prefer a distinct subject format (e.g., `svc-priv-controlplane@acme-financial.com`) and provision them via SCIM as serviceAccount=true. We reserve the `operator` role for runtime operational actions — limited to named service accounts.
- Audits: Private CP ships admin/audit events (authn/authz decisions, role changes, provisioning events) to our audit log store; default retention is 90 days, configurable under an enterprise package.
- Cutover: canary rollout (10% of admin traffic) for 72 hours, with automatic rollback if error rate or auth failures exceed thresholds.

Next steps: please share your Okta metadata and a test SCIM client (or credentials) — Mina will propose a mapping template and a short runbook. 

Best,
Naomi
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
attachments: priv_access_design_v1.pdf (diagram + mapping examples)

Subject: Re: Private CP: SAML/SCIM role mapping and delegated provisioning questions

Thanks Naomi — that direction matches what our ops team expected. Two follow-ups from our side: 

1) Okta specifics: we plan to send you our metadata export — we'll also include the `app_role` claim mapping. Our preference is SCIM push but we need the ability to keep a small set of ICU operator accounts in IdP (non-provisioned) during cutover.
2) Delegated admin: can Redwood support delegated admin scope where we allow a subset of users to administer only particular projects/environments inside Private CP (namespaced roles)?

Can you advise on expected timeline for Mina's mapping template and whether Redwood will accept delta SCIM updates (we prefer deltas vs full push to reduce churn).

Ahmed
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: IT Admin <it-admin@acme-financial.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-17T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private CP: SAML/SCIM role mapping and delegated provisioning questions

Ahmed — hi, Mina from engineering. I've sketched out the mapping and behavior in the attached `scim-mapping.csv` and included a sample SAML metadata header in `saml-metadata.xml` (I referenced both in the design). Key points: 

- Attribute mapping: we accept `urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3` (email), `groups` (array), and `rdw_role` (string). If Okta uses `app_role` we will map it server-side to `rdw_role` at onboarding.
- SCIM: we fully support SCIM 2.0 deltas (PATCH) and bulk operations. Recommended pattern: initial bulk sync (POST) -> incremental PATCH deltas for adds/removes -> periodic reconcile (weekly).
- Role binding: we support namespaced RBAC. SCIM group -> role binding rules are evaluated against resource scope (project/org). Example: group `acme-ops` -> `operator` role scoped to `org:acme-prod`. We expose a `role_binding` SCIM extension to capture scope.
- Delegated admin: yes — our model supports scoping of admin privileges. We recommend using group-based delegation and a `delegated_admin` boolean attribute in SCIM so our control plane treats them as limited administrators.
- Service accounts: mark with `serviceAccount=true` and we will disable interactive SSO flows for those identities; tokens are issued via our service account API.
- Audit hooks: events are emitted to customer-provided syslog/CloudWatch/Splunk endpoints and also stored locally. Retention configurable to 365 days under the enterprise package.

Cutover proposal (high level):
1) Sandbox: basic SAML + test SCIM push to dev instance (1 week)
2) Staged sync: bulk provisioning to staging + verify role bindings (3 days)
3) Canary: route 10% admin traffic and monitor auth/role failures (72 hours)
4) Full switch: enable SCIM authoritative and disable IdP-only group mapping (reserved window)

I'll attach `saml-metadata.xml` example and `scim-mapping.csv` (they're referenced in the attachment list). Happy to run a mapping session with your IdP team.

— Mina
Senior Software Engineer, Identity — Redwood Inference
attachments: saml-metadata.xml, scim-mapping.csv

Subject: Re: Private CP: SAML/SCIM role mapping and delegated provisioning questions — runbook notes

Adding a couple of operational constraints from infra/product: 

- Network: for Private CP in VPC mode we'll need a short list of egress IPs for your Okta SCIM endpoint allowlist; we also recommend VPC peering or PrivateLink for SCIM traffic to reduce surface area.
- Secrets/KMS: service account credentials used for SCIM push should be stored in customer KMS or rotated by our vault integration; we support HSM-backed KMS for high-compliance customers.
- Rollout: canary will be implemented by routing authorization decisions for a subset of operator requests to the new SCIM-authoritative path; if >5% auth failures or >50 auth errors in 1 hour we auto-roll back to IdP-only.
- Monitoring & alerts: we will instrument token exchange and provisioning latencies and emit metrics to your Prometheus stack (or we push to CloudWatch).

I can draft a one-page runbook that lists required artifacts: IdP metadata, SCIM creds, allowlisted egress IPs, service accounts list, and a signed approval window from Acme security.

Karthik
Group Product Manager — Redwood Inference
